name: Queen Kula

related.relation: her council's eldest, who sits by her leave
the dead king she froze into her service

facts.text: Queen Kula is a level-85 hrimthursa giant with 300,000 health, fought together with King Tuscar as the glacier's final.
When she first takes aggro she mocks her own Hrimthursa guardians as useless and arrogant and calls herself merciless and unafraid of death.
At half health she hits harder and casts Thor's Might, a long-range cold blast; she also mesmerizes and roots, and teleports a random attacker to a spot beside her throne.
If Tuscar dies first she fights at full strength from then on (Strength 500 instead of 350).
Allakhazam lists her at level 85 in Tuscaren Glacier; her drops are Ice Queen crowns.
Players in May 2003 said they killed the King and Queen with about 100 people.
The Offline DAoC build turns off the original twin heal (damage to one healing the other) for bot raids.
Bot chat already tells that Kula was the coldest of Bergelmir's line and built her citadel on a dead dragon's bones.

story:
Every skald in Jordheim sings Kula the same way: the youngest and coldest of Bergelmir's line, who stayed in the north when her brothers marched south for green land. Bergelmir was the one giant who lived through the flood when Ymir died, and his children are the hrimthursa, the rime giants, who remember the world before the gods built it. Kula remembers it best. She does not want the gods' world. She wants the one before it, white and still and endless.

She found it in Delling Crater: a dragon dead in the ice, ribs wide as a fjord, so vast that no summer could ever thaw it. She raised her citadel on the bones. She did not ask the Troll Fathers, who were still in their city across the island, and she did not ask the iarn dwarves, who watched her giants cut the first tunnels and went home to their wood very quietly. When a war-band of the dead came up out of the south to take the bones from her, she did not fight it. She froze it, standing, every skeleton with its weapon raised, and gave it orders. Issorden's army still keeps them.

Tuscar came courting with an axe that rang like a bell. She took the axe first, the skalds say, and the smith second, and gave him a throne beside hers and a crown that is mostly a courtesy. He forges; she rules. The Council sits on the ribs because she lets it, and argues for peace because a quiet council costs a queen nothing. The Icelords hold the tunnels because she has never had to ask them twice. Her iceweavers mend the walls each night. Her jailer keeps a cell for every enemy she has named.

She has one law, and she will tell it to you herself when you reach her: only the merciless live through a winter. She despises her own guardians for letting you pass, and says so to your face. Then she fights by her law. She sleeps whoever she dislikes most, roots another where he stands, and reaches out to pull a third across the floor to her throne, so that the raid is always picking itself up. Cut her to half and she stops playing: the cold she brings up then is older than the gods, a blast that reaches across the whole throne room, and her blows land harder. Kill Tuscar first and she does not grieve. She simply has no more reason to hold back.

The skalds who sing her end the song the same way. When the queen of winter dies, they say, the ice will remember her name. Then they look at the door, as if the ice might be listening.
legend: Never split the twins across the room: they stand together and they die together, or not at all. Most raid leaders kill Tuscar first because he hits like his own hammer and his bleed stacks on the tanks; when he falls, Kula hits at full strength for the rest of the fight, so the healers must be fresh for it. Keep cure-mez ready, because she sleeps whoever she dislikes most, and someone on root-break. When she reaches out and pulls someone to her throne, that one runs straight back; don't chase her there. At half she starts the cold blasts, so spread the casters. The old raiders say she has never once looked at the King while fighting, and that if you watch closely when he dies, she smiles.

aggro: You walked past my guardians. They will answer for that. You will answer to me.
Winter keeps only the merciless. Let us see what it keeps of you.
So you got past all my guardians. Useless, every one. I will teach you what they could not.

phases.text: Enough. Feel the cold that was here before your gods.
Tuscar? Then the throne is mine alone. It always was.
Sleep, little summer thing. Dream of green.

death: Bergelmir... I kept the cold... for you...
slay: Another summer creature. They never last.
Lay there. The glacier will keep you.
Merciless lives. You were not merciless.
The glacier keeps everything. It will keep you.

lairEntry: The throne of the rime giants. The air itself is still.
Two thrones. Only one of them is warm with use.
Frost creeps across the floor toward your feet.

phases.text: Queen Kula's breath turns the throne room white!
Kula does not mourn. She grows colder.
The ice queen is dead. The throne room cracks.

atmosphere.realmFirstKill: The Ice Queen has fallen. Tuscaran Glacier is silent.

loremasterTopic.text: The coldest of Bergelmir's line, the skalds say. She built on a dead dragon so no summer could reach her, took [Tuscar] for husband and kept the throne. Her law is that only the merciless survive. Do not expect her to mourn him if he falls first; expect her to fight harder.

bookPage: From 'The Song of the Coldest Daughter', as a skald of Jordheim sings it, set down by Brother Arnulf. Bergelmir rode out the flood of Ymir's blood in a hollow tree, and his children were many, and they were cold. The eldest went south and were burned. The middle ones went east and were drowned. The youngest, Kula, stayed where the ice was, and walked north until she found a death so large that nothing would ever thaw it, and sat down on it. A smith came to her with an axe. She took the axe. A war came to her with an army of bone. She took the army. The skald says one day someone will come to her with nothing, and she will not know what to take.
